ITEM:

Consider a resolution of the City Council of the City of Bedford, Texas, ordering a general election to be held on Saturday, May 7, 2022 for the purpose of electing persons to City Council, Place 3 and Place 5, with a term to expire May 2025; authorizing a contract for election services with Tarrant County; and establishing the dates and times for early voting for such election. | ITEM:

Consider a resolution of the City Council of the City of Bedford, Texas, ordering a general election to be held on Saturday, May 7, 2022 for the purpose of electing persons to City Council, Place 3 and Place 5, with a term to expire May 2025; authorizing a contract for election services with Tarrant County; and establishing the dates and times for early voting for such election.

SUMMARY: | SUMMARY: | SUMMARY: | SUMMARY: | SUMMARY:
BACKGROUND: | BACKGROUND: | BACKGROUND: | BACKGROUND: | BACKGROUND:
This resolution is to order the General Election to be held on May 7, 2022 to elect two City Council members, Place 3 and Place 5, to be filled for three years or until their successors are duly elected and qualified. Pursuant to Section 3.005(c) of the Texas Election Code, a city must order its election no later than the 78th day before Election Day, which this year falls on Friday, February 18, 2022.

Early voting begins Monday, April 25 and runs through Tuesday, May 3. The main early voting location in Bedford will be the Public Library; however, residents can vote at any Tarrant County early voting location. The early voting schedule is below:

                                   
Election Day is 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., Saturday, May 7, 2022. Staff pursued the idea of moving the main Election Day voting location to the Bedford Library; however, the Hurst-Euless-Bedford Independent School District, which splits the costs of elections with the City, was not amenable to that change. To keep costs down and to avoid voter confusion, staff is recommending the Pat May Center at 1849B Central Drive continue to serve as the main Election Day polling location in Bedford as has been done in past years. Residents will be able to vote at any Tarrant County Election Day location. It should be noted, however, that there will be Texas constitutional amendments on the ballot, along with the municipal races. This means that Tarrant County may open more Election Day locations, one of which could be the Library.  
 
A runoff election, if necessary, ensuing from the May 7, 2022 General Election, is tentatively scheduled for June 11, 2022.

As in the past and per state law, staff recommends that this election be held jointly and administered by the Tarrant County Election’s Administration. This has proven to be the most cost effective and efficient way to hold elections.  The exact cost of the election is not known at this time and will depend on how many entities end up contracting with the County.
